rewrites.blindSummary:
This state/province's January 2024 law was the first state/province-wide bathroom ban in the country reaching trans adults, not only school facilities; it remains in force, alongside birth-certificate and surgery requirements for amended markers and a complaint channel for objecting officials.

In May 2025 this state/province became the first state/province to explicitly prohibit flying LGBTQ flags at government buildings and schools (fines up to $500 per day), with similar flag bans following in other state/provinces — its Pride organisation calls the state/province's legislative record the nation's most anti-LGBT.
rewrites.blindTangential: The flag ban and the 2025 Pride-season sponsor exodus are visibility conflicts affecting LGBT+ presence broadly rather than trans status specifically - but they shape the climate a visibly trans visitor encounters, and enforcement of the $500/day flag fines reaches ordinary institutional spaces.
blindSourceSummaries: A news report (29 May 2025) on Pride 2025 in the country: on 7 May this state/province became the first state/province to explicitly prohibit flying LGBTQ+ flags at government buildings and schools, with fines of $500 a day; the local Pride organisation's executive director says the state/province 'leads the nation in anti-LGBTQ legislation'; similar flag bans were signed in two other state/provinces, while one city issued counter-flags and another made the pride flag an official city flag.

A news outlet (30 Jan 2024): the state/province's governor signed the 2024 bill, making this state/province the latest state/province to regulate bathroom access for transgender people; the law requires people to use bathrooms and locker rooms in public schools and government-owned buildings that match their sex assigned at birth. Under the legislation transgender people can defend themselves against complaints by showing documentation of gender-affirming care, and new government buildings must include single-occupant bathrooms. The outlet reported at least 10 other state/provinces had passed similar bathroom-regulation laws by then and quoted a local civil-liberties organisation opposing the bill for risking discriminatory enforcement. This is the dated enactment of the adult-reaching bathroom ban the record attributes to the law.

The state/province legislature's official page for the 2024 bill: the bill's action history shows it was introduced Jan. 11, 2024, advanced through lower- and upper-house committee and floor stages across several substitute versions, and the page's last recorded action is '30 Jan 2024, Governor Signed.' Subject tags cover state/province facilities, K-12 and higher education, and health and human services. Primary state/province-government confirmation of the bill and its Jan. 30, 2024 signing date.

A news outlet documents the reporting mechanism set up under the 2024 law: a form through which residents can report transgender people in 'privacy spaces' such as changing rooms and restrooms, with complainants able to choose whether their names are included while the state/province investigates each 'violation'. The article says the form implements the January 2024 law, which banned trans residents from using bathrooms or competing in a sport that matches their gender identity. This confirms the complaint channel the record lists among this state/province's facility-law provisions.

rewrites.blindSummary:
This state/province's 2023 law makes it a second-degree criminal trespass — up to 60 days — to remain in a public bathroom or changing facility that does not match sex assigned at birth after a government employee orders departure; a civil-liberties organisation calls it 'complex, confusing, and vague' and of limited actual coverage, and among at least 14 state/provinces with facility restrictions only two state/provinces criminalise the act itself.

In March 2025 a 20-year-old trans student was arrested using a women's restroom in the state/province capitol — believed the first arrest anywhere under a state/province bathroom ban. A county judge dismissed the charge in June 2025 on speedy-trial grounds after the state/province missed a 90-day filing deadline; because the arrest was booked as trespass, the ban's constitutionality was never reached. Two rights organisations have issued travel advisories warning of risks to trans travellers and movers.

Physical safety is comparatively better than the law suggests: a July 2026 analysis puts this state/province's recorded killing rate for trans women at 3.7 per 100k per year, below the average of the worst-law state/provinces — itself an undercount floor.
rewrites.blindTangential: Pride and civic visibility are being rolled back state/province-wide — removal of Pride crosswalks, with residents defying the state/province — visibility conflicts affecting LGBT+ presence broadly rather than trans status specifically.
rewrites.blindOutOfScope: The travel advisory itself also cites non-trans laws (reproductive-health restrictions, gun-safety repeals, curriculum censorship); those shape the general rights climate but do not move trans-specific visitor risk.
blindSourceSummaries: A civil-liberties organisation's know-your-rights guide on the 2023 restroom law: refusing to leave a sex-segregated restroom or changing facility can be criminal trespass, but the law only applies in buildings owned or leased by the state/province or local government — state/province offices, courthouses, legislative offices, prisons/jails, local immigration detention, state/province parks and toll-road plazas — and purports to cover all schools, public or private. Private businesses are outside its scope; the organisation advises fact-specific judgment and legal counsel.

A news outlet (2025): a 20-year-old trans college student was arrested at the state/province capitol after declaring an intention to break the law and entering a women's restroom — believed to be the first arrest under this state/province's transgender bathroom restrictions. The student faced a misdemeanor trespass charge punishable by up to 60 days in jail; at least 14 state/provinces have adopted laws barring trans women from women's bathrooms at schools and some government buildings.

A news outlet (6 Jul 2025): on 20 Jun 2025 a county judge threw out the trespass case against the trans student on a legal technicality — as a defendant charged under the facilities law the student had no standing to argue the law itself was illegitimate — so the statute was never substantively tested. The student had been charged 19 Mar 2025 after police, alerted in advance, arrested the student washing hands in a women's restroom at the state/province capitol.

A local rights organisation's travel advisory (12 Apr 2023): the organisation took the 'unprecedented step' of warning about risks to the health, safety and freedom of those considering short or long-term travel or relocation to this state/province, citing laws hostile to LGBTQ people, reproductive-health restrictions, gun-safety rollbacks, and book bans/curriculum censorship. The advisory followed a wave of visitor safety inquiries; the organisation reports events and conferences cancelling and notes the national military considering redeployment for service members' families.

A national law-vs-violence analysis (2008-2025 data): this state/province scores 8.0 on the anti-trans law scale with 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k per year, labelled 'Do Not Travel'; the article's core finding is that state/province law severity does not correlate with killing rates (trendline nearly flat across the 26 state/provinces with data) — legal climate and street-level violence are independent visitor risks.
